words.gram: m. acc. sg., derived title word

hindi: अब इसलिए हम कियन्तःशिरसीय नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter named 'How many in the head' (Kiyantaḥśirasīya).
notes: Prose opening formula, typed as a verse unit in the input. The title is formed from the opening words of unit 3 (kiyantaḥ śirasi) with the suffix -īya.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus indeed spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, typed as a verse unit in the input.

hindi: देहधारियों के सिर में और हृदय में कितने रोग कहे गए हैं? और अनिल आदि के मान के विकल्प से उत्पन्न होने वाले रोग भी कितने हैं?
english: How many diseases are declared in the head and in the heart of embodied beings? And how many diseases of Vāta (anila) and the others are born of variation in measure?
notes: The question begins here and runs to unit 4; the questioner is named Hutāśaveśa in unit 5. māna-vikalpa ('variation in measure') refers to the doṣas being in different degrees; the answer is in units 6 and 41-42.
lines_deva: कियन्तः शिरसि प्रोक्ता रोगा हृदि च देहिनाम्
lines_iast: kiyantaḥ śirasi proktā rogā hṛdi ca dehinām

hindi: हे निष्पाप! कितने क्षय बताए गए हैं, और कितनी पिडकाएँ? और हे दोषों का नाश करने वाले! दोषों की गति कितने प्रकार की कही गई है?
english: How many depletions (kṣaya) are enumerated, and how many boils (piḍakā), O sinless one? And of how many kinds is the course of the doṣas stated to be, O destroyer of doṣas?

text_flags.why: anaga is not a fitting vocative here; anagha 'O sinless one' is the usual address, with only the aspiration lost; the syllable count is unchanged

notes: Both vocatives (anagha, doṣasūdana) are epithets of the teacher addressed; the line does not name him.
lines_deva: क्षयाः कति समाख्याताः पिडकाः कति चानग
lines_iast: kṣayāḥ kati samākhyātāḥ piḍakāḥ kati cānaga

words.gram: m. nom. sg. past act. part. √prach

hindi: हुताशवेश के उस वचन को सुनकर गुरु ने कहा: हे सौम्य! तुमने जो पूछा है, वह मुझसे विस्तार के साथ सुनो।
english: Having heard those words of Hutāśaveśa, the teacher said: 'What you have asked, O gentle one, hear that from me in detail.'
notes: Hutāśaveśa (hutāśa 'fire') is kept as printed, as the name of the questioner of units 3-4.
lines_deva: पृष्टवानसि यत् सौम्य तन्मे शृणु सविस्तरम्
lines_iast: pṛṣṭavānasi yat saumya tanme śṛṇu savistaram

words.gloss: born of variation in the measure of the doṣas

hindi: पाँच शिरोरोग देखे गए हैं, पाँच ही हृदय रोग; दोषों के मान के विकल्प से उत्पन्न होने वाले रोगों की संख्या दो अधिक साठ है।
english: Five head diseases are recognised, and five heart diseases; of diseases born of variation in the measure of the doṣas there are sixty plus two.

text_flags.why: typing error: retroflex ḍ and consonant r (Devanagari ड्र्ष्टाः) for d and vowel ṛ (दृष्टाः); ḍrṣṭāḥ is not a word, dṛṣṭāḥ fits sense and metre

notes: dvyadhikā ṣaṣṭiḥ = sixty-two.

hindi: दस और आठ क्षय हैं, मधुमेह से सम्बन्धित सात पिडकाएँ हैं, और दोषों की गति तीन प्रकार की कही गई है; विस्तार से सुनो।
english: There are ten and eight depletions (kṣaya), seven boils (piḍakā) relating to madhumeha, and the course of the doṣas is stated to be threefold. Hear (them) in detail.
notes: daśa aṣṭau ca = eighteen. madhumeha is kept as the Sanskrit disease name.
lines_deva: दशाष्टौ च क्षयाः सप्त पिडका माधुमेहिकाः
lines_iast: daśāṣṭau ca kṣayāḥ sapta piḍakā mādhumehikāḥ

hindi: रोकने से, दिन में सोने से, रात में जागने से, मद से, ऊँचे स्वर में बोलने से, ओस से, पूर्व की वायु से, अति मैथुन से,
english: From suppression (of urges), from day-sleep, from keeping awake at night, from intoxication, from loud speaking, from dew, from the east wind, from excessive intercourse,
notes: The list of causes runs through units 8-10; the verb is in unit 11. saṃdhāraṇa ('holding back') is read as suppression of natural urges; the object is not stated in the line.

words.gloss: from dust, smoke, snow and sun
from taking heavy, sour and green (food)

hindi: असात्म्य गन्ध के सूँघने से, धूल, धुएँ, हिम और धूप से, भारी, खट्टे और हरित पदार्थों के ग्रहण से, अति शीतल जल के सेवन से,
english: from smelling an unsuitable smell, from dust, smoke, snow and sun, from taking heavy, sour and green (food), from use of very cold water,
notes: ati is printed as a separate word before śītāmbusevanāt; it is read with it ('very cold water' or 'excessive use of cold water'). harita 'green' is read as green herbs or vegetables. gandhād asātmyād āghrātāt: 'from an unsuitable smell (that is) smelled'. ati may also be read with the preceding ādānāt ('from excessive taking of heavy, sour and green food').

words.gloss: from reversal of place and time

hindi: सिर पर आघात से, दूषित आम से, रोने से, आँसुओं को रोकने से, मेघों के आने से, मन के सन्ताप से, देश और काल की विपरीतता से,
english: from injury to the head, from vitiated āma, from weeping, from suppression of tears, from the coming of clouds, from mental distress, from reversal of place and time,

text_flags.why: possible: vāṣpa is a b/v spelling variant of bāṣpa 'tears', which unit 17 prints as bāṣpa; sense unchanged

notes: āma (undigested matter) is kept as Sanskrit. deśakālaviparyaya: unwholesome reversal of the normal character of place and season.

hindi: वात आदि सिर में कुपित हो जाते हैं और रक्त दूषित हो जाता है; तब सिर में विविध लक्षणों वाले रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: Vāta and the others are aggravated in the head and the blood is vitiated; then diseases of various signs arise in the head.
notes: Main clause for the ablatives of units 8-10.

hindi: जहाँ प्राणधारियों के प्राण और सब इन्द्रियाँ आश्रित हैं, और जो अंगों में उत्तम अंग है, वह सिर कहलाता है।
english: That in which the vital breaths (prāṇa) of living beings and all the senses are lodged, and which is the highest of the limbs, is called the head.
lines_deva: प्राणाः प्राणभृतां यत्र श्रिताः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च
lines_iast: prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ yatra śritāḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca

words.gloss: pratiśyā, diseases of mouth, nose, eyes and ears, and giddiness of the head
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva (with tat-puruṣa members)

hindi: अर्धावभेदक हो सकता है, या पूरा सिर दुखता है; प्रतिश्या, मुख, नाक, आँख और कान के रोग, सिर का चकराना,
english: There may be ardhāvabhedaka, or the whole head aches; pratiśyā, diseases of the mouth, nose, eyes and ears, giddiness of the head,
notes: The list continues into unit 14. ardhāvabhedaka and pratiśyā are kept as Sanskrit disease names.
lines_deva: अर्धावभेदको वा स्यात् सर्वं वा रुज्यते शिरः
lines_iast: ardhāvabhedako vā syāt sarvaṃ vā rujyate śiraḥ

words.gloss: stiffness of throat, manyā and jaw
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

words.gloss: arising from Vāta etc. and from worms

hindi: अर्दित, सिर का काँपना, गले, मन्या और हनु की जकड़न, और वात आदि तथा कृमियों से उत्पन्न होने वाले अन्य विविध रोग।
english: ardita, tremor of the head, stiffness of the throat, the manyā (neck) and the jaw, and various other diseases arising from Vāta and the others and from worms.
notes: Continues the list of unit 13; the sense is that these occur in the head. ardita kept as Sanskrit; manyā is the side of the neck.

hindi: परन्तु संग्रह में परम ऋषियों ने जिन पाँच शिरोरोगों को अलग-अलग बताया है, उन्हें उनके अपने-अपने हेतुओं और लक्षणों के साथ मुझसे सुनो।
english: But the five head diseases which have been indicated separately in the summary by the supreme sages, hear those from me with their respective causes and signs.
notes: saṃgraha 'summary' refers to the brief listing (cf. unit 6, 'five head diseases'). hetulakṣaṇa as a dvandva takes the gender of lakṣaṇa (n.).

words.gloss: from loud speaking and excessive speaking

hindi: ऊँचे स्वर में बोलने और अधिक बोलने से, तीक्ष्ण पान से, जागरण से, शीतल वायु के स्पर्श से, मैथुन से, वेगों को रोकने से,
english: From loud speaking and excessive speaking, from sharp drinks, from keeping awake, from contact with cold wind, from sexual intercourse, from suppression of urges,
notes: The causes of Vāta head disease run through units 16-17; the verb is in unit 18. māruta here is physical wind (glossary: physical wind = wind). tīkṣṇapāna: drinking of sharp (strong) drinks.

words.gloss: from tears, grief, fear and fright
from loads, travel and excessive emaciation

hindi: उपवास से, आघात से, अति विरेचन और वमन से, आँसू, शोक, भय और त्रास से, भार, मार्ग-गमन और अति कृशता से,
english: from fasting, from injury, from purgation and emesis in excess, from tears, grief, fear and fright, from (carrying) loads, from travel and from excessive reducing,
notes: abhīghāta is a lengthened form of abhighāta 'injury'. ati at the end of the first line is read with virekād vamanād ('in excess'). bhāra-mārga-atikarśana may also be read 'excessive emaciation from loads and travel'.

hindi: बढ़ी हुई वायु सिर में स्थित सिराओं में प्रवेश करके कुपित होती है; तब उसको वात से बड़ा शूल उत्पन्न होता है।
english: Increased Vāta (vāyu), having entered the vessels (sirā) situated in the head, is aggravated; then from Vāta great pain (śūla) arises for him.
notes: Main clause for the ablatives of units 16-17. śirogatāḥ sirāḥ are taken as f. acc. pl., object of āviśya.

words.gloss: together with the middle of the brows

hindi: दोनों शंख बहुत चुभते हैं, और घाटा भी फटती है; भौंहों के मध्य सहित ललाट, अत्यन्त वेदना से युक्त होकर, मानो जलता है।
english: The two temples (śaṅkha) are intensely pricked, and the nape (ghāṭā) likewise is split; and the forehead together with the middle of the brows, with excessive pain, burns as it were.
notes: Signs of Vāta head disease run through units 19-21.
lines_deva: निस्तुद्येते भृशं शङ्खौ घाटा संभिद्यते तथा
lines_iast: nistudyete bhṛśaṃ śaṅkhau ghāṭā saṃbhidyate tathā

hindi: दोनों कान ध्वनि से आहत होते हैं; दोनों आँखें मानो बाहर खींची जाती हैं; पूरा सिर मानो घूमता है और मानो जोड़ों से छूट जाता है।
english: The two ears are struck with sound; the two eyes are as if pulled out; the whole head as if whirls and is as if loosened from its joints.
notes: vadhyete is read as passive of √vadh 'strike'; svanataḥ is read as svana + -tas 'with sound' (a participle agreeing with the neuter dual śrotre would be svanatī).
lines_deva: घूर्णतीव शिरः सर्वं संधिभ्य इव मुच्यते
lines_iast: ghūrṇatīva śiraḥ sarvaṃ saṃdhibhya iva mucyate

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: सिराओं का जाल अत्यधिक फड़कता है और गर्दन जकड़ जाती है; और अनिलात्मक शिरोरोग में स्निग्ध और उष्ण उपशय देता है।
english: The network of vessels throbs excessively and the neck is stiffened; and in head disease of Vāta (anila) nature what is unctuous and hot gives relief.
notes: upaśete: 'is suitable, gives relief' (upaśaya).

words.gloss: by pungent, sour, salty, alkali, wine, anger, sun and fire

hindi: कटु, अम्ल, लवण, क्षार, मद्य, क्रोध, धूप और अग्नि से सिर में दूषित पित्त शिरोरोग उत्पन्न करता है।
english: By pungent, sour, salty (things), alkali (kṣāra), wine, anger, sun and fire, Pitta vitiated in the head leads to head disease.

hindi: उससे सिर जलता है और दुखता है, शीत …; दोनों आँखें जलती हैं; प्यास, भ्रम और स्वेद उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: By it the head burns and aches; cold …; the two eyes burn; thirst, giddiness and sweating arise.

text_flags.why: possible: suṣūyate is not a recognisable verb form; the sense, parallel to unit 21 (snigdhoṣṇam upaśete for Vāta), calls for a statement that cold gives comfort, which a form such as sukhāyate 'feels pleasant' would give; the reading is not settled
the subject cakṣuṣī is dual, so the verb should be dual dahyete; possible repetition of dahyate from the first line; same syllable count

notes: The second half of line 1 cannot be translated with confidence because of suṣūyate; śītam may be the subject ('cold ...') or object. The flag on dahyate concerns its second occurrence (line 2).
lines_deva: दह्यते रुज्यते तेन शिरः शीतं सुषूयते
दह्यते चक्षुषी तृष्णा भ्रमः स्वेदश्च जायते
lines_iast: dahyate rujyate tena śiraḥ śītaṃ suṣūyate
dahyate cakṣuṣī tṛṣṇā bhramaḥ svedaśca jāyate

words.gloss: by heavy, unctuous food and over-eating

hindi: बैठे रहने के सुखों से, सोने के सुखों से, भारी और स्निग्ध भोजन तथा अति भोजन से सिर में दूषित श्लेष्मा शिरोरोग उत्पन्न करता है।
english: By the pleasures of sitting, by the pleasures of sleep, by heavy and unctuous food and by over-eating, Kapha (śleṣman) vitiated in the head leads to head disease.

text_flags.why: typing error: the vowel e is missing (Devanagari श्ल्ष्मा); śleṣmā is required by sense and by the syllable count of the line

notes: guru-snigdha-ati-bhojanaiḥ may also be read 'by excessive eating of heavy and unctuous (food)'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: उससे सिर मन्द पीड़ा वाला, सुन्न, स्तिमित और भारी हो जाता है; तन्द्रा उत्पन्न होती है, तथा आलस्य और अरोचक भी।
english: By it the head becomes of mild pain, numb, stiff and heavy; drowsiness arises, likewise lassitude and loss of taste (arocaka).

text_flags.why: typing error: rujā 'pain' has a short u; rūja is not a word; the short syllable also suits the fifth syllable of the line

hindi: त्रिदोषज शिरोरोग में वात से शूल, भ्रम और कम्प; पित्त से दाह, मद और प्यास; कफ से भारीपन और तन्द्रा होती है।
english: In head disease born of the three doṣas: from Vāta, pain (śūla), giddiness and tremor; from Pitta, burning, intoxication (mada) and thirst; from Kapha, heaviness and drowsiness.

words.gloss: from eating sesame, milk, jaggery, (food) undigested, putrid and mixed

hindi: तिल, दूध, गुड़, अजीर्ण में, सड़े हुए और संकीर्ण भोजन से, दोषों से भरे हुए मनुष्य के रक्त, कफ और मांस का क्लेद उत्पन्न होता है।
english: From eating sesame, milk and jaggery (guḍa), (eating) while undigested, and putrid and mixed food, excess moisture (kleda) of the blood, Kapha and flesh arises in one abounding in doṣas.
notes: ajīrṇa may mean eating while the previous meal is undigested, or undigested (unwholesome) food; saṅkīrṇa 'mixed' (of incompatible items). Worm head disease is described in units 27-29.

words.gloss: of the one of evil deeds

hindi: तब सिर में क्लेद से उस पापकर्मी के कृमि ऐसा शिरोरोग उत्पन्न करते हैं जिसमें घृणित लक्षण उत्पन्न हो चुके हों।
english: Then, from the excess moisture (saṃkleda) in the head, worms of the evil-doer produce a head disease in which repulsive signs have arisen.

text_flags.why: possible spacing error: jāta has no case ending and can only stand as the first member of the compound jāta-bībhatsa-lakṣaṇam ('with repulsive signs arisen'); the syllable count is unchanged

notes: pāpakarmaṇaḥ is genitive singular: the worms 'of' the person of evil deeds (the patient).

words.gloss: distressed by piercing, cutting pain, itching, swelling and misery
words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: वेधने और काटने की पीड़ा, खुजली, सूजन और दुर्गति से दुःखी व्यक्ति को, और कृमियों के दिखने से, कृमिरोग से पीड़ित जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know (the person) distressed by piercing and cutting pain, itching, swelling and misery as afflicted with worm disease, and (know it) also by the sight of worms.
notes: vyadha-cheda-rujā may be 'pain of piercing and cutting' or 'piercing, cutting and pain'. daurgatya is read as printed ('misery, wretched state'). śopha = swelling (glossary).

words.gloss: by grief, fasting, exercise, and dry, withered and scanty food

hindi: शोक, उपवास, व्यायाम, रूखे, सूखे और थोड़े भोजन से वायु हृदय में प्रवेश करके अत्यन्त पीड़ा उत्पन्न करती है।
english: By grief, fasting, exercise (vyāyāma), and dry, withered and scanty food, Vāta (vāyu), having entered the heart, produces extreme pain.
notes: Heart diseases (units 30-40).

hindi: काँपना, ऐंठन, जकड़न, मूढ़ता, शून्यता और भय, यह वात से पीड़ित के हृदय में रूप है; और भोजन पच जाने पर अत्यधिक वेदना होती है।
english: Trembling, constriction (veṣṭana), stiffness, stupor, emptiness and fear: these are the symptoms in the heart of one afflicted by Vāta; and when (food) is digested, extreme pain.
notes: jīrṇe is read as a locative absolute, 'when (the meal) is digested'; the word 'food' is understood. dara may also mean 'fissure, tearing'; 'fear' is taken here.

words.gloss: by hot, sour, salty, alkali, pungent (food) and eating while undigested

hindi: उष्ण, अम्ल, लवण, क्षार, कटु भोजन और अजीर्ण में भोजन से, तथा मद्य, क्रोध और धूप से, हृदय में पित्त शीघ्र कुपित हो जाता है।
english: By hot, sour, salty, alkali (kṣāra) and pungent food and eating while undigested, and by wine, anger and sun, Pitta is quickly aggravated in the heart.
notes: ajīrṇa-bhojana as in unit 27 (either eating during indigestion or undigested food).

hindi: हृदय में दाह, मुख में तिक्तता, तिक्त और अम्ल डकार, क्लम, प्यास, मूर्च्छा, भ्रम और स्वेद, ये पित्तज हृद्रोग का कारण हैं।
english: Burning in the heart, bitterness in the mouth, bitter and sour eructation, exhaustion (klama), thirst, fainting, giddiness and sweating: (these are) the cause of Pitta heart disease.

text_flags.why: possible: the line lists symptoms, not causes (the causes of Pitta heart disease are in unit 32), so 'sign' (lakṣaṇam) fits the sense; kāraṇam may be repeated from the end of unit 34; same syllable count

english: Over-eating, heavy and unctuous (food), absence of thinking, inactivity and excessive pleasure of sleep: (these are) the cause of Kapha heart disease.

english: In Kapha heart disease, the heart of one beset by drowsiness and loss of taste (aruci) becomes numb, stiff and heavy, as if covered by a stone.

hindi: दो दोषों की प्रबलता और एक दोष की प्रबलता से छः होंगे, और हीन, मध्य और अधिक दोषों से छः, और सम दोषों से एक; ये विकार तेरह सन्निपात हैं।
english: With two (doṣas) predominant and with one predominant there would be six, and with low, middle and high (doṣas) six, and with equal (doṣas) one: these disorders are the thirteen sannipātas (combinations of all three doṣas).
notes: ulbaṇa = predominant. 6 + 6 + 1 = 13. This begins the count of disorders by variation in the measure of the doṣas (units 3 and 6); the counting continues in unit 42.

hindi: संसर्ग में नौ: उनमें से छः एक की वृद्धि से, और तीन सम दोषों से; और उन बढ़े हुए दोषों से अलग-अलग तीन; (इस प्रकार) पच्चीस व्याधियाँ हैं।
english: In combination (saṃsarga, of two doṣas) nine: of them six by the increase of one, three with equal (doṣas); and three separately, by those (doṣas) increased: (thus) twenty-five diseases.
notes: 13 (unit 41) + 9 + 3 = 25. saṃsarga is the combination of two doṣas, sannipāta of all three.
